title: Candidate decoding value
statement: Let $G$ be a regular unique game with alphabet $\text{Fin}(q)$, let each vertex have a finite candidate set, and choose a default label in $\text{Fin}(q)$. The candidate decoding value is the expectation, first over a vertex and then over a neighbor of that vertex, of the candidate decoding edge value.
hypotheses_covered: A regular unique game $G$ with alphabet size $q$
A finite candidate set for each vertex
caveat: The edge value and the probability laws used for both expectations are not defined in the supplied context.
